evidence.field: File summary, source, reuse terms, file history
evidence.text: The exact attached file is named 听-seal.svg. Its description identifies it as 听 in Shuowen seal-script style, cites Sinica Database image 27.542C as its picture source, and gives CC0/public-domain reuse terms. The record identifies the graph as 听; it does not by itself establish that the image is a physical artifact or date the graph’s first use.
evidence.title: File:听-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The distinct file 聽-seal.svg is explicitly described as depicting 聽 in Shuowen seal-script style. This confirms that the attached 听 file and this separate 聽 file are not the same file or character identity.
evidence.title: File:聽-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: B00294 听; received Shuowen analysis and cited literary examples
evidence.text: The entry records the older 听 sense ‘smiling appearance’ and the received analysis 口 with 斤 as phonetic. It cites a Han-period Shanglin fu example and a Tang-period example. These support the association between the 听 graph, its older sense, and the seal-style file identified by Commons; they do not establish the word’s first occurrence or a precise history of the image’s strokes.
evidence.title: [B00294] 听 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03282-011 听 (聽); variants and source citations
evidence.text: The 聽 record lists 听 as a variant, citing Song-Yuan vernacular character sources and a simplified-character correspondence that writes 聽 as 听. Thus 听 has a separate older dictionary entry and is also a form used for 聽; the Song-Yuan citation attests the latter graphic use without proving when it began.
evidence.title: [A03282-011] 听 (聽) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 听 entry; small-seal field, Shuowen text, reading and sense categories
evidence.text: The inspected entry supplies a small-seal image link for 听 and separately lists its Shuowen analysis ‘smiling appearance; from 口, with 斤 phonetic,’ its modern Mandarin alternatives and the later use as simplified 聽. The retrieved text did not expose a directly inspectable glyph image, so the shape was not visually compared here.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the exact 听 file record and Ministry 聽/听 variant record. The Ministry record cites Song-Yuan vernacular uses of 听 for 聽 and separately identifies the standardized simplified correspondence. It does not establish the detailed graphic pathway between the old smiling-word entry and this later use.

search_audit.query: Open CUHK multi-function database 听 entry for small-seal and Shuowen information
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the text view. It provides an image link and entry information for 听, but the glyph pixels were not exposed for visual inspection.

gaps: The Commons SVG page labels the file as 听 and cites a Sinica image record; direct SVG content could not be rendered in the web tool. The source record and the Ministry character entry corroborate the intended identity and association with the old smiling-word entry, but this pass does not independently compare pixel-level SVG content with Sinica’s original image.

The evidence supports describing the selected glyph as a modern Shuowen seal-style rendering associated with the older 听 entry and its received 口 + 斤 analysis. It does not support identifying it as an excavated artifact or as a 聽 glyph.
The age of the depicted small-seal form is an association with the received Shuowen tradition; this research did not inspect an artifact establishing the form’s archaeological date.
